src/model.reason: Model domain types, token usage tracking, and streaming completion contracts; core vocabulary for all provider adapters. effort-updates.ts is the model-layer contract for cache-preserving effort changes shared by the registry, three adapters and Session; no existing file owns that concept. effort-fallback.ts is the retry-once recovery when an endpoint refuses a request carrying such a change; its only importer is provider.ts, which is at its own size ceiling, and effort-updates.ts is imported by the adapters and Session, which should not depend on failure/logging. Lower the ceiling when provider.ts can take it back or the effort files move into a subfolder.

src/protocol.reason: Cross-client event envelopes, serialization codecs, and projection types; stable schemas shared by TUI, headless, and ACP. review-projection.ts is the one public shape of the session's approval review (its live event, the review on an opened request, the read-model list of requests under review), shared by projection, tasks and reducer; folding it into projection.ts or reducer.ts would push either over the line limit and split one contract across two files.

src/session.reason: Session lifecycle, queue and stream ownership plus the two application-context/pricing composition files and three existing host policy helpers moved from engine for #224. The engine is now only portable package contract surfaces; further Session root decomposition remains planned in #197 and Phase 3. effort-timeline.ts derives a turn's effort markers from the log, like a recorded notice; it is a distinct host policy, not part of an existing module.

src/clients/tui/session.tsx.reason: The session wires the composer to the ported legacy menu stack (useMenuStack, double-Escape) and routes every report into the transcript as legacy's addSystemMessage does; that wiring closes over submit, rewind and the viewport, declared later in the same component, so moving it out would add ref plumbing rather than a job seam. The composer's JSX also sits inside ComposerWidth (legacy InputBox's width-0 first frame), which only wraps it, and the command path preserves each menu's composer routing. The approval panel's Escape adds legacy's Stopped line through the viewport (one prop). The approval host also receives the approvals the session is still reviewing, which own the keys as their prompt will (Esc takes over, n denies), so input ownership and the interrupt hook include them (three lines). The menu stack's first-run setup prompt sits under the live divider as legacy BottomArea places it (one line; the gate itself lives in menus/use-first-run-setup.ts). Candidate 2 adds the ported approval prompt host and tasks panel around the hidden composer box (legacy BottomArea order), which the same routing owns. The harness composer acknowledgement waits for the input to remount after an Esc-closed menu (two lines). Issue #221 adds submit-path wiring that has to close over submit's own locals: the /compact branch and the steer-to-auto delivery rule call compactTracker in commands.ts, which owns the in-flight count and outcome notice, and the in-flight draft restore compares against the text as typed so it does not duplicate it. The three submit-capture lines synchronize the actual child image draft before this callback enters submit and records its revision; moving that ordering into a separate helper would couple it back to both the pending-send ref and editor. Lower this ceiling when the composer boundary and its submit callback move together.

They sit beside WireInteraction because clients read them as part of it.

src/session/conversation.ts.reason: The Conversation's turn driver; candidate 2 keeps both the question-cancel notice (a3) and the cross-turn compaction hold (solo/tools), each closing over the same driver state. Direct admission checks foreign native compaction coverage before accepting a turn, using the same configured provider and history as the driver. Eight lines decorate the turn's model history with cache-preserving effort markers (effort-timeline.ts) at the one place a turn's history, new input and settings meet, after admission. Two lines hand notices an earlier process left pending to the background owner (ConversationBackground.deliverReopened) before the turn's history snapshot is taken; the delivery has to precede the turn's admission, so it cannot live in the later notice preparation. Fifteen lines connect the approval arbiter (approval/approval-arbiter.ts): one shared reviewer for root and task approvals built where the generation, accepted history and live publisher meet, handed to each turn and to the task owner, and takeOverReview routed root-then-task exactly like answer. The reviewer's logic stays in the arbiter; only the wiring that closes over this driver's state is here.
